title: Fail-closed web-push fence and orphaned permission code
why: Both rows are classed `LEGACY / UNREACHABLE`, both are Maya-owned, and neither names a capability on its inventory row (`canonicalOwnerSource: REQUIRES SIGNATURE`) — that is why they sit in the 57: "fail-closed stub" is not a capability name. But "already dead" is the wrong reading of S-759. All three legacy Python functions stop on their own first line — the two senders return 0, the subscription lookup returns an empty list, each under the docstring «B24: legacy raw-identity push has no canonical delivery authority» (webhook_server.py:388-390, 393-418) — so they are unreachable **as delivery** while remaining live code that live paths still enter and are refused by: the staff-chat reply consults the subscription lookup (webhook_server.py:5057, reached from the registered `POST /api/chat`), and the loyalty cashback job calls the client sender (loyalty.py:369, reached from the registered `loyalty` job). The row calls them "fences, not features", ratchet-frozen — so removing them is an AUTHORITY change carrying a negative test, not a cleanup. S-762 is the genuinely orphaned half: `window.requestPushPermission` (native-enhancements.js:205-234) requests permission and subscribes, and no file in this tree calls it or loads the script. That grep is not the probe the row asks for — the shipping front end is hand-uploaded to Beget and the deployed copy is not in this tree — so removal still owes a recorded check, because a second permission-requesting path nobody knows about is precisely how a consent prompt reappears unowned. Wave 1 decides the owner label only; both rows carry the same parity requirement, "a recorded unreachability probe, not an assumption".
disappear: Nothing in Wave 1 — no code is removed, no fence is lifted, and no successor is named for either row, so nothing here is replaced by anything. Both rows are still marked not retirable, and deletion is deferred to K16 under an explicit condition: RETIRE IN K16 **after the probe is recorded**. Signing this group as attribution is therefore not signing that deletion.
remain: The fail-closed behaviour, unchanged: the two Python senders keep returning 0, the subscription lookup keeps returning an empty list, and the browser function stays unreferenced. That freeze is machine-checked rather than conventional — a runtime guard asserts each of the three bodies is still exactly `return 0` / `return []` and reports the adapter as missing if a function is deleted (package5_control_plane_runtime_guard.py:500) — which is why these are not lines anyone can quietly tidy away. What also remains is what the fence leaves standing in front of a master: the staff-chat answer still states that new bookings, reschedules, cancellations and tips arrive by push, then ends on «Сейчас push-подписки нет — откройте приложение и нажмите «Включить уведомления»» (webhook_server.py:5069-5073), an instruction that cannot produce a subscription while the fence holds. This group neither fixes nor schedules that. And the rows' own debt remains: no canonical owner on either (both `REQUIRES SIGNATURE`), no successor, and no unreachability probe recorded — so "unreachable" is still a classification rather than a measured fact. Both rows stay in K16 with that debt attached.
risk: LOW — for what Wave 1 actually does: attach an owner label to two rows while removing nothing and moving no authority. That rating covers the attribution only and must not be read as a rating of the K16 deletion this group defers to. S-759's removal is an authority change needing the recorded probe, a negative test, and an amendment to the runtime guard that pins those bodies; S-762's removal needs a recorded check that nothing calls or loads it, including on the hand-uploaded Beget front that is not in this tree. Each is re-rated then, on its own evidence. No frozen limitation is contradicted or leaned on: nothing here rests on STEP_UP_VERIFIED, on Gate 10 being enforced, or on approval being separation of duties; no surface in this group claims a client confirmed attendance; and this local push fence is not one of the fundamental rules, so it neither improves nor is covered by the 13-of-21 fail-closed record.
user_impact: No user notices a change — Wave 1 attaches an owner label and removes nothing. But the rows are not "already inert", and the silence is broader than push. S-759 is live: `_push_subscriptions_for_master` (webhook_server.py:388-390) is called at :5057 inside `_master_chat_shortcut`, which two staff-mode chat handlers reach (:7032, :7584), so a master who asks about «пуш/уведомления» gets a live answer that asserts master push works and — because the stub always returns [] — always ends on «Сейчас push-подписки нет — откройте приложение и нажмите "Включить уведомления"», an instruction that can never produce a subscription while the fence stands. O04 neither fixes nor schedules that string. On the client side `_send_client_push` returns 0 (webhook_server.py:405-418) with three live callers, not two: :532 («Вы записаны ✅ / Запись перенесена 🔁 / Запись отменена ❌»), :476 (post-visit tip offer) and loyalty.py:369 (loyalty-care offer); because the stub returns before doing anything, it also drops the `persist_in_chat=True` in-chat cards (mybookings / tips / loyalty widgets), so the client loses the chat message as well as the push. `_send_master_push` is the only genuinely inert half — it has no production caller at all. For S-762, no page in the repository loads `native-enhancements.js` (the only references are inside the file's own header), so `window.requestPushPermission` is unreachable in this snapshot; state that as not-yet-probed rather than as fact, since the row's own parityRequirement demands «a recorded unreachability probe, not an assumption» and the Beget front is uploaded by hand. Before and after Wave 1 the behaviour is identical.
security_impact: NONE in Wave 1 — nothing is removed, no check moves from client to server, and both fences keep failing closed exactly as they do now. Direction note for the K16 deletion this group defers to: S-759 is not inert dead code but a load-bearing fail-closed fence, and the runtime reach is uneven — `_send_client_push` is reached from three live callers (webhook_server.py:532, :476, loyalty.py:369) and refuses delivery that would otherwise be addressed from a raw phone→chat_id lookup (`database.find_client_by_phone`, which still executes ahead of the fence) with no canonical delivery authority («B24: legacy raw-identity push has no canonical delivery authority»); `_push_subscriptions_for_master` is reached on a live staff-chat path (:5057) but only as a count; `_send_master_push` has no production caller and is held open solely by the ratchet. The freeze is machine-enforced, not conventional: `package5_control_plane_runtime_guard.py:500` asserts each body is exactly `return 0` / `return []` and reports «fail-closed adapter missing» if the function is gone, and `test_package5_b24_web_push.py` re-injects a `webpush()` call and requires the scan to fail. So removing S-759 is an authority change that must amend that guard contract as well as carry a negative test — not a cleanup. S-762 is neutral today and closes nothing, since that path never runs; its eventual removal would be a small hardening (it deletes a second, unowned permission-prompt/subscribe path that could mint a push subscription outside the owned consent path), but that benefit is contingent on the unreachability probe the row still requires — claiming it before the probe is recorded is an assumption, not a finding. No frozen limitation is touched: nothing here rests on STEP_UP, on Gate 10 being enforced, or on approval being separation-of-duties.
